description:
FILED s543v (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, base 38420fae = MAIN-READY-115 + records, v2-16600; found while writing #5464's guard row).

THE SHAPE (neutral reproducer, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on the base and the s543v tree):

    our @x = (1, 2);
    print "a @::x b @main::x c @x\n";     # perl a 1 2 b 1 2 c 1 2    PCL a @::x b 1 2 c 1 2
    print "d $::x[1] e ${::x}[0]\n";      # both d 2 e 1

Only the ARRAY spelling `@::name` inside a double-quoted string is left as text; the scalar `$::x[1]`, the braced `${::x}[0]` and the qualified `@main::x` interpolate.  Where to look: the string scanner's array-name arm (Pl/InterpScan.pm -- interpolation scanning happens there or not at all, docs/interp-scan.md): the `::` package-less qualifier is accepted for `$` but not for `@`.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): `./pl2cl` of the one line -- if the emitted string is the literal `"a @::x b "`, it is the scanner, not the runtime.

LABEL: silent (rare).
frequency_reason: found by s543v's own guard row; no Rosetta program, no lib/ or everyday/ file holds the spelling (grep -F '"@::'); the `::` short form of main is unusual inside a string
subject: SILENT WRONG: `"@::name"` (the main-package array written with the empty package) is not interpolated in a string -- `our @x = (1,2); print "@::x"` prints the text `@::x` where perl prints `1 2`; `"@main::x"`, `"$::x[1]"` and `"${::x}[0]"` are right
triage_reason: string interpolation of a package array is core language (perlop "Gory details of parsing quoted constructs"); IN by docs/supported-subset.md section 3
